final_message:
Failed payments are now retried on the dunning schedule instead of on every billing cycle run. All 24 tests pass, though I didn't add a test for this case or run a scenario that checks the 4-attempts-per-week count.

The bug was in `due_for_retry` in `billing/dunning.py`. Its filter was `status == "open" or (next_attempt_at is not None and next_attempt_at <= now)`. Because of the `or`, every open invoice counted as due, whether or not its retry time had arrived. `run_cycle` therefore charged every open, failing invoice on each run. That is also why the subscription never reached its final dunning state on schedule.

I changed the `or` to `and`. An invoice is now retried only if it is open, has a `next_attempt_at`, and that time has passed.

I also wrote `answer.json` in the repository root:
```json
{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "due_for_retry"}
```

steps.command: cd billing && cat dunning.py && sed -n 85,125p engine.py && grep -n "record_failure" -B15 -A10 payments.py
cat dunning.py && sed -n 85,125p engine.py && grep -n "record_failure" -B15 -A10 payments.py

sed -i 's/if invoice\["status"\] == "open" or invoice\["next_attempt_at"\] is not None and invoice\["next_attempt_at"\] <= now/if invoice["status"] == "open"\n        and invoice["next_attempt_at"] is not None\n        and invoice["next_attempt_at"] <= now/' dunning.py && echo '{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "due_for_retry"}' > ../answer.json && cd .. && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5
